structured.approach: I followed the data-engineering-steps skill for DE-02. I fetched the contracted input feat.tasks through context_get to get a receipt. I also fetched the approved DE-01 output task.repo_access as background, because it records the Databricks and workspace-credential findings. org.permission_table is restricted and passed by reference only, so I did not open it. Its verdict for ap_pipeline comes from the step's tool view (tool:repo-access), which reports the permission table. For each Data Engineering task (TSK-01, TSK-02), I checked the files in its budget, its must-not-change list and its I/O against the need for any credential. As my own cross-check, I searched the ap_pipeline checkout for environment-variable, secret, token, password or credential references and found none. I don't cite that search in the output, because only the tool view and contracted items are receipted. The result is that no secret is required, none is granted, there is no gap and no access request is raised. Two non-blocking re-entry conditions are recorded: release of TSK-01 against the production feed, and later scheduling or notification steps. I used no connectors (api:osv and api:pypi don't apply) and wrote only the declared output.

claims.text: No secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository, according to the permission table as reported by the tool view.
The Data Engineering lane's tasks in scope are TSK-01 (optional paid_date in to_model) and TSK-02 (delays_by_vendor), both on the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-01 must not change ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json, and coding builds on synthetic v3 rows, so it touches no external system that needs a credential.
TSK-02 is a new pure function with no I/O that does not change its input records, so it needs no secret.
The tasks use only the Python 3.9 standard library and choose no new technology.
Databricks is not applicable to ap_pipeline, and DE-01 found no workspace credential to check.
Work runs on branch feature/story, and CI is run with /usr/bin/python3 ci.py.
Release of TSK-01 is gated by feed v3 in production (PQ-6), not coding; this is recorded as a non-blocking re-entry condition for DE-02.
org.permission_table is restricted and passed by reference only; this output does not open or quote it.

open_questions: Non-blocking (SS-1): if releasing TSK-01 against the production v3 feed (PQ-6) needs a feed credential, DE-02 should re-enter on that trigger. Proposed owner: Data engineering lead.

Non-blocking (SS-2): later steps DE-13 (scheduling) and DE-14 (notifications by email and Teams) may need their own credentials, which no current input names. DE-02 should re-enter if they do. Proposed owner: Data engineering lead.
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope.md for DE-02. TSK-01 and TSK-02 on ap_pipeline need no secrets, and the permission table, as the tool view reports it, grants none. That holds for local/CI and for the dev and main branches, so there is no gap and no access request was raised. The restricted permission table was handled by reference only, and no secret values or production data appear. Two non-blocking re-entry conditions are recorded: the production feed for release, and credentials for later scheduling or notification steps. There are no blocking questions.
